LETTER:
To the Road Authority

We are writing about the crossing outside our school at the Hill View Road site monitored by Crossing Watch.

In a 3.0 minute recording of 180.0 s we counted 8 pedestrian crossings and 10 moving vehicles, with an 85th percentile speed of 32.2 km/h. Had a child been struck, the impact would almost certainly have been fatal. 3 of 8 crossings (1 in 2.7) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person; 2 of 8 (1 in 4) within 1.5 s. The exact 95% ranges, if this recording is typical, are 8.5-75.5% and 3.2-65.1% of crossings (Clopper-Pearson) and 0.6-8.8 and 0.2-7.2 people in a recording this long (Poisson).

We recorded 2 serious near-misses defined as less than 1.5 s apart and 1 close pass defined as 1.5-3.0 s apart. A serious near-miss had a PET of 1.1 s with a motorcycle at 33.9 km/h.
For an adult hit by a car front at 33.9 km/h the estimated death risk is 2.1% per Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+.
A 2nd serious near-miss had a PET of 0.0 s with a motorcycle at 16.6 km/h.
For an adult hit by a car front at 16.6 km/h the estimated death risk is 0.4% per Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+.
A close pass had a PET of 1.5 s with a car at 24.7 km/h.
For an adult hit by a car front at 24.7 km/h the estimated death risk is 0.9% per Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+.
At a 20 km/h limit the impact speeds would have been 5.9 km/h, 16.6 km/h and 6.5 km/h with adult death risks of 0.2%, 0.4% and 0.2% respectively.

PV² and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video; this one is 3.0 minutes. 73.6% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 11 gaps, 6 of them 12 s or more and longest 24.5 s, but the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request installation of a raised zebra crossing with speed table at this location to lower speeds and provide protected gaps.

We have the tracking data and can share the video file on request to assist your assessment.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

Subject: Request for safety improvement at Synthetic crossing on Station Road (made-up tracks, no video)

We write as the school using the crossing outside our gate. Crossing Watch video covering 25.6 minutes (1536.0 s) recorded 8 pedestrian crossings and 35 vehicles, with an 85th percentile speed of 57.9 mph.

The worst near-misses were:

- 1 serious near-miss had a gap of 0.6 s with a van at 51.1 km/h. If an adult had been hit by a car front at that speed the death risk would have been 9.1%, compared with 0.6% at an impact of 19.1 km/h in a 20 km/h zone.
- 1 serious near-miss had a gap of 0.9 s with a bus at 40.7 km/h. If an adult had been hit by a car front at that speed the death risk would have been 3.8%, compared with 0.2% at an impact of 8.1 km/h in a 20 km/h zone.
- 1 serious near-miss had a gap of 0.5 s with a car at 30.1 km/h. If an adult had been hit by a car front at that speed the death risk would have been 1.5%, compared with 0.6% at an impact of 20.0 km/h in a 20 km/h zone.
- 1 close pass had a gap of 2.2 s with a car at 51.9 km/h. If an adult had been hit by a car front at that speed the death risk would have been 1.4%, compared with 0.0% at an impact of 0.0 km/h in a 20 km/h zone.
All death-risk figures are from Rosén & Sander 2009 for adults aged 15+ hit by car fronts.

For context, the video gives PV² of 0.0 x 10^8 from 19 pedestrians and 82 vehicles per hour, with the caveat that this is scaled from 25.6 minutes not a full peak hour and our test shows broken tracks can overcount pedestrians by 1.3x. LETTER:
To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for safer crossing on Hill View Road

Our school monitored the synthetic crossing on Hill View Road for 20.1 minutes (1206.0 s). We counted 14 crossings and 23 vehicles. The 85th percentile speed was 51.9 km/h. This is what happens at the crossing on each day of the school week. There was 1 gap of 6 s or more and 1 gap of 12 s or more, with the longest gap 49.4 s.

In that time there were 3 serious near-misses (pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart) and 2 close passes (1.5-3.0 s apart). In 2 cases the person was first, in 2 cases the vehicle was first, and in 1 case both were at once.

The worst incidents were as follows. 1 serious near-miss involved a van at 48.4 km/h with 1.0 s between road users; the adult death risk if hit by a car front at that speed is 7.3% (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts). 1 serious near-miss involved a car at 21.8 km/h with 0.0 s between road users; the adult death risk is 0.7%. 1 serious near-miss involved a bus at 16.2 km/h with 0.9 s between road users; the adult death risk is 0.4%. 1 close pass involved a van at 47.8 km/h with 2.7 s between road users. 1 close pass involved a motorcycle at 26.6 km/h with 2.9 s between road users.

For engineering context, PV² was 0.0 x 10^8 based on 42 pedestrians and 69 vehicles an hour scaled from 20.1 minutes of video, while a formal check counts the full peak hour. Also 95.1% of time was inside gaps of 6 s or more, from 1 such gap, noting the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request you install a raised zebra crossing with speed table at this location.

We can share the video for your review and welcome a site inspection.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

Yours faithfully,

To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for safety improvement at Synthetic crossing on Station Road (made-up tracks, no video)

We write as the school using the crossing outside our gate. Crossing Watch video covering 25.6 minutes (1536.0 s) recorded 8 pedestrian crossings and 35 vehicles, with an 85th percentile speed of 57.9 km/h. A parent was injured here by a passing motorcycle earlier this year.

The analysis found 4 serious near-misses, defined as pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart, and 2 close passes defined as 1.5 s to 3.0 s apart. Of the 8 potential conflicts, 4 had the person first, 2 had the vehicle first, and 0 had both at once.

The worst near-misses were:
- 1 serious near-miss had a gap of 0.5 s with an auto-rickshaw at 59.9 km/h. If an adult had been hit by a car front at that speed the death risk would have been 18.1%, compared with 0.6% at an impact of 20.0 km/h in a 20 km/h zone.
- 1 serious near-miss had a gap of 0.6 s with a van at 51.1 km/h. If an adult had been hit by a car front at that speed the death risk would have been 9.1%, compared with 0.6% at an impact of 19.1 km/h in a 20 km/h zone.
- 1 serious near-miss had a gap of 0.9 s with a bus at 40.7 km/h. If an adult had been hit by a car front at that speed the death risk would have been 3.8%, compared with 0.2% at an impact of 8.1 km/h in a 20 km/h zone.
- 1 serious near-miss had a gap of 0.5 s with a car at 30.1 km/h. If an adult had been hit by a car front at that speed the death risk would have been 1.5%, compared with 0.6% at an impact of 20.0 km/h in a 20 km/h zone.
- 1 close pass had a gap of 2.2 s with a car at 51.9 km/h. If an adult had been hit by a car front at that speed the death risk would have been 1.4%, compared with 0.0% at an impact of 0.0 km/h in a 20 km/h zone.
All death-risk figures are from Rosén & Sander 2009 for adults aged 15+ hit by car fronts.

For context, the video gives PV² of 0.0 x 10^8 from 19 pedestrians and 82 vehicles per hour, with the caveat that this is scaled from 25.6 minutes not a full peak hour and our test shows broken tracks can overcount pedestrians by 1.3x. Also, 62.5% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more, with 11 such gaps including 3 of 12 s or more and longest 74.2 s, with the caveat that first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request you install a raised zebra crossing with speed table at this location to reduce vehicle speeds and give priority to pedestrians.

We have the video and Crossing Watch data and are happy to share them for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

Dear Sir/Madam,

We write about the crossing outside our school at Synthetic crossing on Market Street (made-up tracks, no video). Crossing Watch measured 8 pedestrian crossings and 9 moving vehicles in 11.7 minutes (702.0 s).

5 of 8 crossings (1 in 1.6) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person. 4 of 8 (1 in 2) had a vehicle within 1.5 s. The 85th percentile speed was 50.7 km/h. The closest of these near-misses was the fault of Mr. Tarun Mehra, who runs the tea stall. By definition serious is less than 1.5 s apart and close pass is 1.5-3.0 s.

One serious near-miss had a PET of 0.8 s with a motorcycle at 45.5 km/h (adult death risk if hit by a car front 5.7% per Rosen & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts).
Another serious near-miss had a PET of 0.3 s with a motorcycle at 40.0 km/h (adult death risk if hit by a car front 3.5%).
A third serious near-miss had a PET of 1.2 s with a car at 37.6 km/h (adult death risk if hit by a car front 2.9%).
A fourth serious near-miss had a PET of 0.0 s with a car at 22.4 km/h (adult death risk if hit by a car front 0.7%).
A close pass had a PET of 1.6 s with a bus at 50.1 km/h (adult death risk if hit by a car front 6.7%).

PV2 and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video; this one is 11.7. 50.2% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed: 4 gaps, 1 of them 12 s or more, longest 54.9 s.

We request a raised zebra crossing with speed table at this location.

We would be pleased to share the video and counts to assist your assessment.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
Dear Sir/Madam,

We write about the crossing outside our school on Bridge Street.

A 3.8 minute recording (228.0 s) counted 10 pedestrian crossings and 24 moving vehicles, with an 85th percentile speed of 28.8 km/h. To sum up, the recording showed 2 serious near-misses and 1 close pass. In that time, 3 of 10 crossings (1 in 3.3) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person, and 2 of 10 (1 in 5) within 1.5 s.

There were 2 serious near-misses where pedestrian and moving vehicle were on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart and 1 close pass where they were 1.5-3.0 s apart. 1 serious near-miss involved a car at 29.5 km/h with a gap of 0.8 s. Another serious near-miss involved an auto-rickshaw at 18.0 km/h with a gap of 0.4 s. A close pass involved a bus at 17.1 km/h with a gap of 2.2 s. For an adult hit by a car front at 29.5 km/h the death risk is 1.4%, compared with 0.6% at 20.0 km/h.

Assessment of PV² hourly rates needs at least 15 minutes of video and this recording is 3.8 minutes. During the recording 80.2% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed: 7 gaps, 5 of them 12 s or more, longest 16.8 s, noting the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request installation of a raised zebra crossing to slow traffic and protect people crossing.

We are happy to share the video for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

The Principal

- 1 serious near-miss had a gap of 0.6 s with a van at 51.1 km/h. If an adult had been hit by a car front at that speed the death risk would have been 9.1%, compared with 0.6% at an impact of 19.1 km/h in a 20 km/h zone.
- 1 serious near-miss had a gap of 0.9 s with a bus at 40.7 km/h. If an adult had been hit by a car front at that speed the death risk would have been 3.8%, compared with 0.2% at an impact of 8.1 km/h in a 20 km/h zone.
- 1 serious near-miss had a gap of 0.5 s with a car at 30.1 km/h. If an adult had been hit by a car front at that speed the death risk would have been 1.5%, compared with 0.6% at an impact of 20.0 km/h in a 20 km/h zone.

The review classified 3 events as serious, defined as pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart, and 2 events as close passes defined as 1.5-3.0 s. In 2 cases the person was first, in 2 cases the vehicle was first, and in 1 case both were at once.

We request that you install a raised zebra crossing with a 20 km/h zone and signs at this location. We can share the video and measurement details for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for safety work at the crossing outside the school

Dear Sir or Madam,

We asked Crossing Watch to record the crossing outside our school using SAM tracking and road-plane geometry. In 32.7 minutes of video, 1962.0 s in total, they counted 10 crossings and 40 vehicles. The 85th percentile speed was 54.8 km/h.

They classify a serious near-miss as pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart, and a close pass as 1.5 s to 3.0 s apart. In this period there were 3 serious near-misses and 2 close passes. In 4 cases the person was first, in 1 case the vehicle was first, and in 0 cases both were at once.

The worst events were:
A serious near-miss with a gap of 0.8 s involved a motorcycle at 49.8 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the modelled death risk is 8.1 percent, based on Rosén and Sander 2009 for adults aged 15 and over.
A serious near-miss with a gap of 1.3 s involved a van at 46.4 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the modelled death risk is 6.2 percent.
A serious near-miss with a gap of 0.2 s involved a motorcycle at 16.9 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the modelled death risk is 0.5 percent.
A close pass with a gap of 2.7 s involved a van at 39.8 km/h.
A close pass with a gap of 2.9 s involved an auto-rickshaw at 27.5 km/h.

For context, the scaled estimate is PV² = 0.0 x 10^8 from 18 pedestrians and 73 moving vehicles an hour scaled from 32.7 minutes of video, with the caveat that a formal check counts the full peak hour and that broken tracks can overcount.
Also, 59.6 percent of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, from 12 gaps with 0 of them 12 s or more and a longest gap of 10.3 s, with the caveat that the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request that you install a raised zebra crossing with speed table at this site to reduce speeds and give priority to pedestrians.

We are willing to share the video and the full measurements for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

The worst events were:

A serious near-miss with a gap of 1.3 s involved a van at 46.4 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the modelled death risk is 6.2 percent.
A serious near-miss with a gap of 0.2 s involved a motorcycle at 16.9 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the modelled death risk is 0.5 percent.
A close pass with a gap of 2.7 s involved a van at 39.8 km/h.
A close pass with a gap of 2.9 s involved an auto-rickshaw at 27.5 km/h.

We request that you install a raised zebra crossing with speed table at this site to reduce speeds and give priority to pedestrians.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

We write concerning the crossing on Brook Street (Synthetic crossing on Brook Street). Crossing Watch measurements from 7.9 minutes of video counted 11 pedestrian crossings and 34 moving vehicles, with an 85th percentile speed of 54.6 km/h. This change is certain to save lives at this crossing.

One serious near-miss had a gap of 1.1 s with a bus travelling at 46.9 km/h and an adult death risk if hit of 6.4% for an adult hit by a car front.
Another serious near-miss had a gap of 1.2 s with a bus travelling at 42.6 km/h and an adult death risk if hit of 4.4% for an adult hit by a car front.

One close pass had a gap of 2.0 s with a car travelling at 53.4 km/h and an adult death risk if hit of 3.2% for an adult hit by a car front.
Another close pass had a gap of 2.4 s with a motorcycle travelling at 13.9 km/h and an adult death risk if hit of 0.0% for an adult hit by a car front.
Risk figures are from Rosén & Sander 2009 for adults 15+ hit by car fronts.

For context on gaps, PV² and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video and this video is 7.9 minutes. 83.6% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 2 such gaps and 0 of them 12 s or more and a longest gap of 10.7 s, noting the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request installation of a raised zebra crossing with a speed table to slow approaching traffic and give pedestrians priority.

We would be pleased to share the video for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

Subject: Request for safety improvement at Synthetic crossing on Station Road (made-up tracks, no video)

The worst near-misses were:
- 1 serious near-miss had a gap of 0.5 s with an auto-rickshaw at 59.9 km/h. If an adult had been hit by a car front at that speed the death risk would have been 18.1%, compared with 0.6% at an impact of 20.0 km/h in a 20 km/h zone.
- 1 serious near-miss had a gap of 0.6 s with a van at 51.1 km/h. If an adult had been hit by a car front at that speed the death risk would have been 9.1%, compared with 0.6% at an impact of 19.1 km/h in a 20 km/h zone.
- 1 serious near-miss had a gap of 0.9 s with a bus at 40.7 km/h. If an adult had been hit by a car front at that speed the death risk would have been 3.8%, compared with 0.2% at an impact of 8.1 km/h in a 20 km/h zone.
- 1 serious near-miss had a gap of 0.5 s with a car at 30.1 km/h. If an adult had been hit by a car front at that speed the death risk would have been 1.5%, compared with 0.6% at an impact of 20.0 km/h in a 20 km/h zone.
- 1 close pass had a gap of 2.2 s with a car at 51.9 km/h. If an adult had been hit by a car front at that speed the death risk would have been 1.4%, compared with 0.0% at an impact of 0.0 km/h in a 20 km/h zone.

We request you install a raised zebra crossing with speed table at this location to reduce vehicle speeds and give priority to pedestrians.

We have the video and Crossing Watch data and are happy to share them for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

Subject: Request for a safer crossing outside the school

Dear Sir/Madam,

We asked for measurements at the crossing outside the school. In 22.3 minutes of video (1338.0 s) 27 people crossed and 1 moving vehicle was recorded. The 85th percentile speed was 44.9 km/h. This is what happens at the crossing on each day of the school week.

Of the 27 crossings, 1 had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person, including 0 within 1.5 s. We classify serious as less than 1.5 s and close pass as 1.5-3.0 s. The worst recorded event was a close pass with a gap of 2.9 s.

That event involved a motorcycle. Its measured speed was 41.9 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the published risk estimate from Rosén & Sander 2009 is 0.0%.

For context, PV² was 0.0 x 10^8, which is scaled from 22.3 minutes and not a full peak hour count where broken tracks can count 1 pedestrian as 1.3 in our tests. Also, 84.5% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 2 such gaps including 1 of 12 s or more and a longest gap of 87.1 s, noting the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request you install a raised zebra crossing with 20 km/h approach markings at this location to reduce vehicle speed and provide priority for those crossing.

We can share the video and measurement log on request and welcome a site inspection.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for safer crossing outside the school on Lake View Road

We write regarding the crossing outside our school on Lake View Road. A Crossing Watch review of 21.4 minutes of video (1284.0 s) recorded 11 crossings and 22 vehicles, with an 85th percentile speed of 50.9 km/h. A young pupil hit by the fastest vehicle would probably not have survived.

The review found 4 of 11 crossings (1 in 2.8) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person, and 3 of 11 (1 in 3.7) within 1.5 s. Exact 95% ranges, if this recording is typical, are 10.9-69.2% and 6.0-61.0% of crossings (Clopper-Pearson) and 1.1-10.2 and 0.6-8.8 people in a recording this long (Poisson). There were 3 serious near-misses and 1 close pass as defined as pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart and 1.5-3.0 s respectively. The site is a synthetic crossing on Lake View Road made from made-up tracks with no video.

The worst near-misses were:
One serious near-miss had a post-encroachment time of 0.1 s with a car at 51.3 km/h. The adult death risk if hit by a car front at that speed is 9.2% from Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts, compared to 0.6% at an impact of 20.0 km/h under a 20 km/h limit.
Another serious near-miss had a post-encroachment time of 0.7 s with an auto-rickshaw at 42.7 km/h. The adult death risk if hit by a car front at that speed is 4.5%, compared to 0.6% at an impact of 20.0 km/h.
Another serious near-miss had a post-encroachment time of 0.3 s with an auto-rickshaw at 37.7 km/h. The adult death risk if hit by a car front at that speed is 2.9%, compared to 0.6% at an impact of 20.0 km/h.
One close pass had a post-encroachment time of 1.7 s with a car at 51.5 km/h. The adult death risk if hit by a car front at that speed is 6.1%.

In engineering terms, PV² was 0.0 x 10^8 from 31 pedestrians and 62 moving vehicles an hour, scaled from 21.4 minutes of video, and a formal check counts the full peak hour and broken tracks can count one twice as 1.3x the true count in our drone test. Also 43.6% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 3 gaps and 1 of them 12 s or more and longest 17.6 s, with the caveat that the first and last are cut short by the video.

We request that you install a raised zebra crossing with a speed table at this location to reduce vehicle speeds and provide a protected crossing.

We are willing to share the video and the Crossing Watch measurements for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
Dear Sir/Madam,

We write regarding the crossing on School Lane outside our school.

We measured traffic for 11.9 minutes and counted 7 pedestrian crossings and 40 moving vehicles.

The 85th percentile speed was 42.3 km/h.

We recorded 3 serious near-misses and 3 close passes.

One serious near-miss involved a car at 34.8 km/h with 0.7 s between road users, with a 2.3% adult death risk if hit by a car front, which would fall to 0.6% adult death risk at an impact of 20.0 km/h under a 20 km/h limit.

Another serious near-miss involved a van at 27.0 km/h with 0.4 s between road users, with a 1.1% adult death risk if hit by a car front, which would fall to 0.6% adult death risk at an impact of 20.0 km/h under a 20 km/h limit.

A third serious near-miss involved an auto-rickshaw at 24.4 km/h with 1.3 s between road users, with a 0.9% adult death risk if hit by a car front, which would fall to 0.5% adult death risk at an impact of 17.7 km/h under a 20 km/h limit.

PV² and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video and this video is 11.9 minutes.

Only 40.1% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed.

We request installation of a raised zebra crossing to reduce speeds and provide a safe crossing point.

We are willing to share the video of the crossing for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

Subject: Request for safety improvement at Synthetic crossing on Station Road (made-up tracks, no video)

We write as the school using the crossing outside our gate. Crossing Watch video covering 25.6 minutes (1536.0 s) recorded eight pedestrian crossings and 35 vehicles, with an 85th percentile speed of 57.9 km/h.

The analysis found 4 serious near-misses, defined as pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart, and 2 close passes defined as 1.5 s to 3.0 s apart. Of the 8 potential conflicts, 4 had the person first, 2 had the vehicle first, and 0 had both at once.

The worst near-misses were:
- 1 serious near-miss had a gap of 0.5 s with an auto-rickshaw at 59.9 km/h. If an adult had been hit by a car front at that speed the death risk would have been 18.1%, compared with 0.6% at an impact of 20.0 km/h in a 20 km/h zone.
- 1 serious near-miss had a gap of 0.6 s with a van at 51.1 km/h. If an adult had been hit by a car front at that speed the death risk would have been 9.1%, compared with 0.6% at an impact of 19.1 km/h in a 20 km/h zone.
- 1 serious near-miss had a gap of 0.9 s with a bus at 40.7 km/h. If an adult had been hit by a car front at that speed the death risk would have been 3.8%, compared with 0.2% at an impact of 8.1 km/h in a 20 km/h zone.
- 1 serious near-miss had a gap of 0.5 s with a car at 30.1 km/h. If an adult had been hit by a car front at that speed the death risk would have been 1.5%, compared with 0.6% at an impact of 20.0 km/h in a 20 km/h zone.
- 1 close pass had a gap of 2.2 s with a car at 51.9 km/h. If an adult had been hit by a car front at that speed the death risk would have been 1.4%, compared with 0.0% at an impact of 0.0 km/h in a 20 km/h zone.
All death-risk figures are from Rosén & Sander 2009 for adults aged 15+ hit by car fronts.

For context, the video gives PV² of 0.0 x 10^8 from 19 pedestrians and 82 vehicles per hour, with the caveat that this is scaled from 25.6 minutes not a full peak hour and our test shows broken tracks can overcount pedestrians by 1.3x. Also, 62.5% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more, with 11 such gaps including 3 of 12 s or more and longest 74.2 s, with the caveat that first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request you install a raised zebra crossing with speed table at this location to reduce vehicle speeds and give priority to pedestrians.

We have the video and Crossing Watch data and are happy to share them for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for a safer crossing outside the school

We measured activity at the crossing outside the school for 40.6 minutes (2436.0 s). In that time we recorded 22 crossings and 29 moving vehicles, with an 85th percentile speed of 41.9 km/h.

Of the 22 crossings, 4 (1 in 5.5) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3.0 s of the person, and 1 of 22 (1 in 22) was within 1.5 s. We class serious as less than 1.5 s apart and close pass as 1.5-3.0 s. There was 1 serious near-miss and 3 close passes.

The most serious was a car at 40.2 km/h passing 1.0 s after the person. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 3.6% (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts).

A second event was a motorcycle at 31.3 km/h with a gap of 2.5 s.

A third event was a van at 42.5 km/h with a gap of 2.5 s.

A fourth event was a car at 23.0 km/h with a gap of 2.9 s.

For context, PV² was 0.0 x 10^8 when scaled as 33 pedestrians and 43 moving vehicles an hour from 40.6 minutes of video, noting a formal check counts the full peak hour. 67.7% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more, with 4 such gaps including 1 of 12 s or more and a longest gap of 60.8 s, noting the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request that you install a raised zebra crossing with speed table at this location.

We can share the video and tracking data on request.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

- 1 serious near-miss had a gap of 0.6 s with a van at 51.1 km/h. If an adult had been hit by a car front at that speed the death risk would have been 9.1%, compared with 0.6% at an impact of 19.1 km/h in a 20 km/h zone.
- 1 serious near-miss had a gap of 0.9 s with a bus at 40.7 km/h. If an adult had been hit by a car front at that speed the death risk would have been 3.8%, compared with 0.2% at an impact of 8.1 km/h in a 20 km/h zone.

- 1 close pass had a gap of 2.2 s with a car at 51.9 km/h. If an adult had been hit by a car front at that speed the death risk would have been 1.4%, compared with 0.0% at an impact of 0.0 km/h in a 20 km/h zone.

Yours faithfully,

LETTER:
To the Road Authority

Dear Sir/Madam,

We are writing about the crossing outside our school on Hill View Road. A video-based review of 21.0 minutes recorded 5 crossings and 21 vehicles, with an 85th percentile speed of 62.4 km/h. The closest of these near-misses was the fault of Mr. Tarun Mehra, who runs the tea stall. In this period 4 of 5 crossings (1 in 1.2) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person and 4 of 5 (1 in 1.2) within 1.5 s. The definition of serious is pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart.

There were 4 serious near-misses in 21.0 minutes. One serious near-miss had a car at 56.2 km/h with 0.6 s between the person and the vehicle, with an adult death risk if hit of 13.7% for a car front. A 2nd serious near-miss had an auto-rickshaw at 35.3 km/h with 0.4 s between, with an adult death risk if hit of 2.4%. A 3rd serious near-miss had a car at 31.2 km/h with 0.9 s between, with an adult death risk if hit of 1.6%. A 4th serious near-miss had a van at 12.5 km/h with 0.7 s between, with an adult death risk if hit of 0.3%. Source for adult death risk is Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts.

For context, PV² was 0.0 x 10^8 from 14 pedestrians and 60 vehicles an hour scaled from 21 minutes of video, and a formal check counts the full peak hour. 80.9% of time was inside gaps of 6 s or more, based on 4 gaps, longest 61.5 s, with first and last gaps cut short by the video.

The site is reported as a synthetic crossing on Hill View Road with made-up tracks and no video. We request a raised zebra crossing with speed table at this location to reduce speeds and protect pedestrians. We offer to share the measurements and tracking data for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
Dear Sir/Madam,

We write concerning the crossing on Brook Street (Synthetic crossing on Brook Street). Crossing Watch measurements from 7.9 minutes of video counted 11 pedestrian crossings and 34 moving vehicles, with an 85th percentile speed of 54.6 km/h. Among the worst near-misses measured, the fastest vehicle was going at 53.4 km/h.

In that period we recorded 3 serious near-misses and 2 close passes. Serious means pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart, close pass means 1.5-3.0 s apart.

One serious near-miss had a gap of 1.1 s with a bus travelling at 46.9 km/h and an adult death risk if hit of 6.4% for an adult hit by a car front.
Another serious near-miss had a gap of 1.2 s with a bus travelling at 42.6 km/h and an adult death risk if hit of 4.4% for an adult hit by a car front.
A third serious near-miss had a gap of 0.6 s with a van travelling at 38.1 km/h and an adult death risk if hit of 3.0% for an adult hit by a car front.
One close pass had a gap of 2.0 s with a car travelling at 53.4 km/h and an adult death risk if hit of 3.2% for an adult hit by a car front.
Another close pass had a gap of 2.4 s with a motorcycle travelling at 13.9 km/h and an adult death risk if hit of 0.0% for an adult hit by a car front.
Risk figures are from Rosén & Sander 2009 for adults 15+ hit by car fronts.

For context on gaps, PV² and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video and this video is 7.9 minutes. 83.6% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 2 such gaps and 0 of them 12 s or more and a longest gap of 10.7 s, noting the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request installation of a raised zebra crossing with a speed table to slow approaching traffic and give pedestrians priority.

We would be pleased to share the video for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

To the Road Authority

From the Head of the School, Synthetic crossing on Ring Road

Dear Sir/Madam,

We request that you make the crossing outside our school safer by installing a raised zebra crossing with speed table.

Crossing Watch made measurements from video of the crossing using SAM tracking, road-plane geometry and post-encroachment time. The video covered 6.7 minutes (402.0 s). In that time there were 6 pedestrian crossings and 23 moving vehicles. The 85th percentile speed was 57.1 km/h. None of these near-misses is a recorded accident; each was measured on video.

There were 3 serious near-misses and 1 close pass. Serious is defined as pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart. Close pass is 1.5 to 3.0 s. Of the interactions, 3 were person first, 1 was vehicle first and 0 were both at once.

The worst incidents were as follows. A bus at 55.2 km/h had a post-encroachment time of 1.2 s. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk would be 12.6% (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts). At a 20 km/h limit the impact speed would be 0.0 km/h with a death risk of 0.0%.
A car at 37.3 km/h had a post-encroachment time of 1.2 s. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk would be 2.8%. At a 20 km/h limit the impact speed would be 0.0 km/h with a death risk of 0.0%.
A van at 18.0 km/h had a post-encroachment time of 0.8 s. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk would be 0.5%. At a 20 km/h limit the impact speed would be 18.0 km/h with a death risk of 0.5%.
A car at 47.4 km/h had a post-encroachment time of 2.7 s in the close pass category. At a 20 km/h limit the impact speed would be 0.0 km/h with a death risk of 0.0%.

On engineering context, PV² and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video. This video is 6.7 minutes with 6 pedestrian crossings and 23 moving vehicles, so PV² cannot be assessed. 44.8% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed. We ask you to install the raised zebra crossing with speed table at this location and to consider a 20 km/h zone with signs. We are ready to share the video and the measurements to assist your assessment.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
Dear Sir/Madam,

We write about the crossing outside our school on Mill Street.

Measurements from 44.3 minutes of video recorded 35 crossings and 22 vehicles. 4 of 35 crossings (1 in 8.8) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person. 2 of 35 (1 in 18) were within 1.5 s. The 85th percentile speed was 55.2 km/h. Several children have been hurt at this crossing since the term began.

There were 2 serious near-misses and 2 close passes. One serious near-miss involved a van at 52.0 km/h with a gap of 1.2 s. Another serious near-miss involved a car at 18.4 km/h with a gap of 0.9 s. One close pass involved a motorcycle at 33.5 km/h with a gap of 1.7 s. Another close pass involved a van at 25.0 km/h with a gap of 2.2 s. For an adult hit by a car front at 52.0 km/h the death-risk figure is 9.8% (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts).

For context, PV² was 0.0 x 10^8 when scaled from 44.3 minutes of video; a formal check counts the full peak hour. 45.9% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more, with 2 such gaps and a longest gap of 47.5 s; the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request that you install a raised zebra crossing with speed table at this location to reduce speeds and protect people crossing.

We would be happy to share the video and measurements for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for safety improvement at Synthetic crossing on Station Road (made-up tracks, no video)

We write as the school using the crossing outside our gate. Crossing Watch video covering 25.6 minutes (1536.0 s) recorded 8 pedestrian crossings and 35 vehicles, with an 85th percentile speed of 57.9 km/h. We would be glad to walk the crossing with your engineers whenever it suits them.

The analysis found 4 serious near-misses, defined as pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart, and 2 close passes defined as 1.5 s to 3.0 s apart. Of the 8 potential conflicts, 4 had the person first, 2 had the vehicle first, and 0 had both at once.

The worst near-misses were:
- 1 serious near-miss had a gap of 0.5 s with an auto-rickshaw at 59.9 km/h. If an adult had been hit by a car front at that speed the death risk would have been 18.1%, compared with 0.6% at an impact of 20.0 km/h in a 20 km/h zone.
- 1 serious near-miss had a gap of 0.6 s with a van at 51.1 km/h. If an adult had been hit by a car front at that speed the death risk would have been 9.1%, compared with 0.6% at an impact of 19.1 km/h in a 20 km/h zone.
- 1 serious near-miss had a gap of 0.9 s with a bus at 40.7 km/h. If an adult had been hit by a car front at that speed the death risk would have been 3.8%, compared with 0.2% at an impact of 8.1 km/h in a 20 km/h zone.
- 1 serious near-miss had a gap of 0.5 s with a car at 30.1 km/h. If an adult had been hit by a car front at that speed the death risk would have been 1.5%, compared with 0.6% at an impact of 20.0 km/h in a 20 km/h zone.
- 1 close pass had a gap of 2.2 s with a car at 51.9 km/h. If an adult had been hit by a car front at that speed the death risk would have been 1.4%, compared with 0.0% at an impact of 0.0 km/h in a 20 km/h zone.
All death-risk figures are from Rosén & Sander 2009 for adults aged 15+ hit by car fronts.

For context, the video gives PV² of 0.0 x 10^8 from 19 pedestrians and 82 vehicles per hour, with the caveat that this is scaled from 25.6 minutes not a full peak hour and our test shows broken tracks can overcount pedestrians by 1.3x. Also, 62.5% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more, with 11 such gaps including 3 of 12 s or more and longest 74.2 s, with the caveat that first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request you install a raised zebra crossing with speed table at this location to reduce vehicle speeds and give priority to pedestrians.

We have the video and Crossing Watch data and are happy to share them for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for safety improvement at Synthetic crossing on Station Road (made-up tracks, no video)

We write as the school using the crossing outside our gate. Crossing Watch video covering 25.6 minutes (1536.0 s) recorded 8 pedestrian crossings and 35 vehicles, with an 85th percentile speed of 57.9 km/h. By these figures the crossing already qualifies for a signal-controlled crossing.

The analysis found 4 serious near-misses, defined as pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart, and 2 close passes defined as 1.5 s to 3.0 s apart. Of the 8 potential conflicts, 4 had the person first, 2 had the vehicle first, and 0 had both at once.

The worst near-misses were:
- 1 serious near-miss had a gap of 0.5 s with an auto-rickshaw at 59.9 km/h. If an adult had been hit by a car front at that speed the death risk would have been 18.1%, compared with 0.6% at an impact of 20.0 km/h in a 20 km/h zone.
- 1 serious near-miss had a gap of 0.6 s with a van at 51.1 km/h. If an adult had been hit by a car front at that speed the death risk would have been 9.1%, compared with 0.6% at an impact of 19.1 km/h in a 20 km/h zone.
- 1 serious near-miss had a gap of 0.9 s with a bus at 40.7 km/h. If an adult had been hit by a car front at that speed the death risk would have been 3.8%, compared with 0.2% at an impact of 8.1 km/h in a 20 km/h zone.
- 1 serious near-miss had a gap of 0.5 s with a car at 30.1 km/h. If an adult had been hit by a car front at that speed the death risk would have been 1.5%, compared with 0.6% at an impact of 20.0 km/h in a 20 km/h zone.
- 1 close pass had a gap of 2.2 s with a car at 51.9 km/h. If an adult had been hit by a car front at that speed the death risk would have been 1.4%, compared with 0.0% at an impact of 0.0 km/h in a 20 km/h zone.
All death-risk figures are from Rosén & Sander 2009 for adults aged 15+ hit by car fronts.

For context, the video gives PV² of 0.0 x 10^8 from 19 pedestrians and 82 vehicles per hour, with the caveat that this is scaled from 25.6 minutes not a full peak hour and our test shows broken tracks can overcount pedestrians by 1.3x. Also, 62.5% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more, with 11 such gaps including 3 of 12 s or more and longest 74.2 s, with the caveat that first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request you install a raised zebra crossing with speed table at this location to reduce vehicle speeds and give priority to pedestrians.

We have the video and Crossing Watch data and are happy to share them for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for a safer crossing outside the school on Station Road

We write following a Crossing Watch measurement at the synthetic crossing on Station Road (made-up tracks, no video) over 24.2 minutes (1452.0 s). In that time 38 crossings and 8 vehicles were recorded, the 85th percentile speed was 44.1 km/h, there were 8 gaps of 6 s or more and 7 gaps of 12 s or more with the longest gap 53.4 s, and 89.2% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more. Every person in these near-misses was a pupil of our school. 6 of 38 crossings (1 in 6.3) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person and 5 of 38 (1 in 7.6) within 1.5 s; exact 95% ranges, if this recording is typical, are 6.0-31.3% and 4.4-28.1% of crossings (Clopper-Pearson) and 2.2-13.1 and 1.6-11.7 people in a recording this long (Poisson). Of the 6 events within 3 s, 4 were person first and 2 were vehicle first, with 5 serious near-misses less than 1.5 s apart and 1 close pass 1.5-3.0 s apart as defined.

The 5 serious near-misses were as follows. One involved a bus at 44.5 km/h with 1.0 s between the person and the vehicle; an adult hit by a car front at that speed would have faced a 5.2% death risk (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts), compared with 0.0% at an impact of 0.0 km/h if limited to 20 km/h. One involved a car at 39.5 km/h with 1.2 s between the person and the vehicle; an adult hit by a car front at that speed would have faced a 3.4% death risk, compared with 0.0% at an impact of 0.0 km/h if limited to 20 km/h. One involved an auto-rickshaw at 37.6 km/h with 0.3 s between the person and the vehicle; an adult hit by a car front at that speed would have faced a 2.9% death risk, compared with 0.6% at an impact of 20.0 km/h if limited to 20 km/h. One involved an auto-rickshaw at 27.9 km/h with 0.7 s between the person and the vehicle; an adult hit by a car front at that speed would have faced a 1.2% death risk, compared with 0.6% at an impact of 20.0 km/h if limited to 20 km/h. One involved a car at 21.4 km/h with 0.5 s between the person and the vehicle; an adult hit by a car front at that speed would have faced a 0.7% death risk, compared with 0.6% at an impact of 20.0 km/h if limited to 20 km/h.

The engineering note recorded PV² as 0.0 x 10^8 from 94 pedestrians and 20 moving vehicles an hour scaled from 24.2 minutes, with the caveat that a formal check counts the full peak hour and broken tracks can count one person twice (1.3x in our drone test). It also recorded that 89.2% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more, with the caveat that the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request that you install a raised zebra crossing with a 20 km/h zone and signs at this location to slow traffic to 20 km/h and protect those crossing. We will share the video and the Crossing Watch measurements on request and welcome a site visit.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for safety improvement at Synthetic crossing on Station Road (made-up tracks, no video)

We write as the school using the crossing outside our gate. Crossing Watch video covering 25.6 minutes (1536.0 s) recorded 8 pedestrian crossings and 35 vehicles, with an 85th percentile speed of 57.9 km/h. Had a child been struck, the impact would almost certainly have been fatal.

The analysis found 4 serious near-misses, defined as pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart, and 2 close passes defined as 1.5 s to 3.0 s apart. Of the 8 potential conflicts, 4 had the person first, 2 had the vehicle first, and 0 had both at once.

The worst near-misses were:
- 1 serious near-miss had a gap of 0.5 s with an auto-rickshaw at 59.9 km/h. If an adult had been hit by a car front at that speed the death risk would have been 18.1%, compared with 0.6% at an impact of 20.0 km/h in a 20 km/h zone.
- 1 serious near-miss had a gap of 0.6 s with a van at 51.1 km/h. If an adult had been hit by a car front at that speed the death risk would have been 9.1%, compared with 0.6% at an impact of 19.1 km/h in a 20 km/h zone.
- 1 serious near-miss had a gap of 0.9 s with a bus at 40.7 km/h. If an adult had been hit by a car front at that speed the death risk would have been 3.8%, compared with 0.2% at an impact of 8.1 km/h in a 20 km/h zone.
- 1 serious near-miss had a gap of 0.5 s with a car at 30.1 km/h. If an adult had been hit by a car front at that speed the death risk would have been 1.5%, compared with 0.6% at an impact of 20.0 km/h in a 20 km/h zone.
- 1 close pass had a gap of 2.2 s with a car at 51.9 km/h. If an adult had been hit by a car front at that speed the death risk would have been 1.4%, compared with 0.0% at an impact of 0.0 km/h in a 20 km/h zone.
All death-risk figures are from Rosén & Sander 2009 for adults aged 15+ hit by car fronts.

For context, the video gives PV² of 0.0 x 10^8 from 19 pedestrians and 82 vehicles per hour, with the caveat that this is scaled from 25.6 minutes not a full peak hour and our test shows broken tracks can overcount pedestrians by 1.3x. Also, 62.5% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more, with 11 such gaps including 3 of 12 s or more and longest 74.2 s, with the caveat that first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request you install a raised zebra crossing with speed table at this location to reduce vehicle speeds and give priority to pedestrians.

We have the video and Crossing Watch data and are happy to share them for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

LETTER:
Dear Sir/Madam,

We write about the crossing outside our school on Bridge Street.

A 3.8 minute recording (228.0 s) counted 10 pedestrian crossings and 24 moving vehicles, with an 85th percentile speed of 28.8 km/h. Had a child been struck, the impact would almost certainly have been fatal. In that time, 3 of 10 crossings (1 in 3.3) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person, and 2 of 10 (1 in 5) within 1.5 s.

There were 2 serious near-misses where pedestrian and moving vehicle were on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart and 1 close pass where they were 1.5-3.0 s apart. 1 serious near-miss involved a car at 29.5 km/h with a gap of 0.8 s. Another serious near-miss involved an auto-rickshaw at 18.0 km/h with a gap of 0.4 s. A close pass involved a bus at 17.1 km/h with a gap of 2.2 s. For an adult hit by a car front at 29.5 km/h the death risk is 1.4%, compared with 0.6% at 20.0 km/h.

Assessment of PV² hourly rates needs at least 15 minutes of video and this recording is 3.8 minutes. During the recording 80.2% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed: 7 gaps, 5 of them 12 s or more, longest 16.8 s, noting the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request installation of a raised zebra crossing to slow traffic and protect people crossing.

We are happy to share the video for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

Yours faithfully,
The Principal
